parsed.explanation: Combined regime shows state threat-framing, police venue raids, and escalating vigilante attacks on trans women tied by reporting to a 2025 defence decree, plus one documented trans traveller death in custody amid an alleged $100,000 extortion demand. Sexuality/morality laws are selective but documented as a police lever. No execution or routine imprisonment for trans presentation is documented, and enforcement varies subnationally, placing this above severe 0.15 profiles but in high-risk 0.25 territory.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border document, X-marker, scanner or entry-screening practice for trans visitors is documented.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented visitor-facing border protection is provided.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Venue raid arrested 75 people in June 2025. A foreign trans traveller arrested Aug 2022 died in custody; mother alleged beating and $100,000 demand, police denied violence. Aceh religious police impose caning, including for gender disorder.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police regulation from 2009 and 2015 hate-speech circular exist, but outcomes are not sourced. No effective remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or raid can lead to custody where extortion and death-in-custody risk were documented for a traveller, with dispute unresolved.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No universal bathroom or facility ban documented. Subnational local rules have fined trans women, and Aceh applies its own Islamic code with religious-police caning.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National police have sometimes refused local rules conflicting with national guarantees, showing uneven application.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Exposure varies sharply by province/city; national-level morality provisions interact with Aceh/South Sumatra criminalisation.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No emergency ward, medication, or care-access practice for visitors is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: New penal code effective Jan 2026 penalises extra-marital sex up to 2 years, reaching same-sex relations, selectively prosecuted. Pornography law up to 7 years. Oct 2025 decree frames LGBTQ+ people as defence threats to monitor/control.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No specific anti-discrimination/harassment protection as of record; constitutional employment guarantee is theoretical and contradicted by documented discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses vigilante and police action; selective morality law provides a lever against visibly gender-nonconforming visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-specific entry, custody, care or family-travel rule for minors is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor would face the same undocumented border/custody environment as adults; no separate mitigation is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 reporting describes vigilante mobs attacking trans women, tied to officials' rhetoric and defence decree. Discriminatory arrests documented since 2016; 94 LGBT cases documented by umbrella organisation in 2026 reporting.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented effective prosecution of attackers or protection for victims; government mostly silent after 2016 pathologisation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Official framing correlates with street violence, suggesting state tolerance rather than protection when outed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate with denominator; custody death allegation contested; enforcement of police protections unsourced; 2025 online-content bill status unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Job-offer rescission after human-rights advice shows occasional institutional correction, but no visitor remedy system documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns do not offset documented raids, vigilante escalation and custody death; absence of rate data is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: police raids on gatherings, custody harassment/extortion risk, officials framing trans people as deceivers/threats, no death-penalty for presentation documented. This case adds a contested traveller death in custody, keeping it at 0.25 level.

Lower/safer than this case: 0.35-C has police extortion stops but local recognition and serving shopkeepers. Here vigilante mob attacks, a defence decree, mass venue raid, and custody death show broader state-tolerated targeting.

Higher/safer than 0.15-B: no militia systematically detaining/beating travellers in transport corridors, no routine imprisonment/sentence pattern documented, and prosecution is described as selective rather than systematic.

Materially below 0.45: that anchor has a universal facility rule but police prosecution of an assault and no organised targeting. Here targeting, raids and threat-framing are documented and remedies are not shown to work.

parsed.synthesis: If outed, a visitor faces layered exposure: morality/sexuality law selectively enforced, police raids, vigilante violence amplified by official defence threat-framing, uneven subnational religious-police punishment including caning in Aceh, and documented custody danger for a trans traveller. Protections are paper-only or unsourced, and no remedy is shown to change outcomes. This is organised/state-tolerated targeting below the near-certain imprisonment of 0.15, hence high risk around 0.26.
